key_highlights: ASX shed $90bn in a week as rate-rise fears and oil price surge pressured miners and banks (Headlines 26, 51)
Iron ore entering 'bloodletting' phase, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX (Headline 32)
Oil prices 'explode' as suppression fails; Australian fuel prices set to rise 30c, stoking inflation fears (Headlines 21, 40)
AUD 'smashed' on growth scare; RBA flagged rental inflation as key concern (Headlines 38, 49)
Housing correction accelerates at high end while affordable segment remains resilient; first-home buyers surge (Headlines 42, 75)
Gas policy shift: Australia softens local supply rules, Albo 'sells out' gas reservation, easing Asian fears (Headlines 30, 52, 71)
Chinese inflation soars, adding external demand risk for commodity exporters (Headline 64)
Mining cap-raise activity intensifies via Canaccord; small-caps PolarX, Sunstone Metals, Manuka Resources in focus (Headlines 17, 27)

sectors.trend: Sharp negative. Iron ore 'bloodletting' underway; oil surge benefits energy names but weighs on broad mining. Cap-raise activity signals capital stress in juniors.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from falling iron ore. Gold names (Kuniko, Gateway WA) may benefit from safe-haven flows. Canaccord-led cap raises (Headline 27) dilute equity holders.

sectors.trend: Negative. Rate-rise fears and growth scare pressure NAB.AX, CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX. Bond yields rising but credit-risk concerns offset margin gains.
sectors.implications: Net interest margins may widen but loan-loss provisions could rise if growth slows. Superannuation policy debate (Headlines 28, 44, 74) adds regulatory uncertainty.

sectors.trend: Mixed-to-positive. Oil surge benefits Santos (STO.AX) and Woodside (WDS.AX) upstream. Gas policy liberalisation (Headlines 30, 52, 71) supports domestic gas producers but raises geopolitical questions.
sectors.implications: Fuel price pass-through (30c rise) pressures downstream refiners and transport. Gas reservation sale may attract Asian infrastructure capital.

sectors.trend: Negative. Woolworths (WES.AX) price increases during 'Price Freeze' erode trust. Fuel costs and tax burden squeeze household budgets. Clothing chain closes 177 stores.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, CSG.AX face margin pressure. Consumer discretionary names under pressure. 'Drowning in taxes' narrative (Headline 31) may drive political risk.

sectors.trend: Negative at high end, resilient at affordable end. Housing price crash at premium segment; first-home buyers surge. RBA rental inflation concern (Headline 49) pressures residential REITs.
sectors.implications: Residential REITs (e.g., GPT.AX, ICPS.AX) face occupancy and yield pressure. Commercial REITs may benefit from rate stabilisation. Migrant-driven demand (Headline 62) is a structural tailwind.

sectors.trend: Neutral-to-positive. CSL.AX and Medtronic (MDT) heart-device growth provide defensive appeal. HIVE/BUZZ HPC AI cloud expansion (Headline 37) signals small-cap tech momentum.
sectors.implications: Defensive rotation into CSL.AX, SGH.AX likely in risk-off environment. Small-cap tech (Iondrive, Neurizon – Headline 20) offers speculative upside.

key_themes: Oil price surge and fuel inflation as primary macro driver
RBA rate-path uncertainty and rental inflation focus
Iron ore price correction pressuring ASX 200 heavyweight miners
AUD weakness amplifying import costs and inflation
Housing market bifurcation: high-end correction vs affordable resilience
Gas policy liberalisation and Asian energy security
Chinese inflation and demand risk for commodity exporters
Superannuation policy populism vs institutional integrity
Mining sector capital raises signalling stress in juniors

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Oil-driven inflation and RBA rate hike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge with energy long exposure; reduce rate-sensitive REIT and property allocations; monitor RBA statement for forward guidance.
Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX weightings; rotate into gold (Kuniko, Gateway WA) and battery-tech (Critical Resources) for diversification.
Favour domestic-revenue companies; avoid AUD-sensitive importers; consider AUD/USD options for hedging.
Monitor high-end vs affordable divergence; residential REITs at risk; construction and materials names may see short-term demand drop.
Diversify away from China-exposed commodity names; monitor Chinese inflation data (Headline 64) for demand signals.
Track One Nation and populist proposals (Headlines 28, 44, 74); super fund managers (HUB.AX, PPA.AX) face regulatory risk.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and battery-tech miners as safe-haven and structural growth plays
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore bloodletting and AUD weakness support gold; Critical Resources battery tech passing month-long test signals commercial viability

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy upstream exposure on oil surge
opportunities.rationale: Oil 'explodes' as suppression fails; Santos and Woodside benefit from higher realised prices; gas policy liberalisation adds optionality

opportunities.recommendation: Defensive tilt into healthcare and consumer staples
opportunities.rationale: Risk-off rotation; CSL.AX and CSL-linked names offer earnings visibility; WES.AX pricing power despite 'Price Freeze' breach

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce or hedge iron ore-heavy mining exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore 'bloodletting' and Chinese inflation suggest demand softening; BHP/RIO/FMG face 10-15% downside risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim residential REIT and high-end property exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Steepest price falls at premium end; RBA rental inflation concern may prompt further tightening; housing correction 'has further to run'

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash or short-duration bonds as rate uncertainty persists
defensive_moves.rationale: Late-stage bubble warning (Headline 22) and $90bn ASX drawdown suggest elevated volatility; bond yields rising but direction uncertain

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. ASX likely to test lower supports as oil-driven inflation forces RBA hawkish pivot. Miners and banks remain under pressure. AUD weakness amplifies import costs. Expect 3-5% further downside on ^AXJO over 1-3 months unless oil stabilises.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. Housing correction at high end may stabilise by H2 2027; gas policy liberalisation supports energy sector; battery-tech and gold offer structural growth. RBA likely to peak rates within 6 months, enabling re-rating of rate-sensitive sectors.
